html:
"Georgian Kingdom" is the map's label, for 700, for the Georgian lands of the time, mainly the Principality of Iberia, or Kartli, in eastern Georgia, along with the Georgian west.

Iberia had been a kingdom and had become Christian in the 300s; see Conversion of Georgia. The Persians abolished its monarchy around 580, and local princes then ruled under Persian or Byzantine overlords. In the west, Lazica stayed close to the Byzantine Empire.

From the 640s the Arabs of the Caliphate came north. They held Tbilisi, which became seat of an emirate, and the princes paid tribute. The Georgians were caught between the Caliphate, Byzantium and the Khazars. Out of these princely lands the Bagrationi family later built the united Kingdom of Georgia around 1008.
sum: "Georgian Kingdom" is the map's label, for 700, for the Georgian lands of the time, mainly the Principality of Iberia, or Kartli, in eastern Georgia, along with the Georgian west.
